traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309: perianth biseriate, uniseriate or absent (formula K 5 [0] C 5 [0]); Floral Diagrams p. 259 adds that petals are often missing and Euphorbia's cyathium flowers are naked. A single sepal whorl is mapped to 'tepals'.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 259: merism mostly 4- or 5-merous, ranging from 3 to 8; Simpson p. 307 says generally 5-merous.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309: Simpson's formula: ovary of 3 carpels, rarely 2 to many (Floral Diagrams p. 257 general formula: 3, rarely 1 or up to 20).

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309: gynoecium syncarpous with a superior ovary.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 133 Euphorbiaceae: herbs, shrubs or trees, some with milky sap; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or compound, sometimes reduced, mostly with stipules; flowers unisexual, mostly both sexes on one plant; petals mostly absent; stamens from one to a thousand; ovary mostly of three cells; fruit a capsule or a drupe. Hutchinson's family also holds what APG sets apart as Phyllanthaceae and Picrodendraceae; only characters that hold for the narrower family are stated, and the perianth (sepals only in most, none in Euphorbia's cyathium) is left for a value the vocabulary has.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310, family Euphorbiaceae: inflorescence cyme, usually; read as {"cyme": "usually"}.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310, family Euphorbiaceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic, usually; read as {"actinomorphic": "usually"}.
